Repository instructions: Follow `RULES.md` strictly for coding quality, validation, lint budgets, and definition of done. Repo tooling and explicit user instructions override this file. For concrete requests, start with relevant files; otherwise inspect relevant top-level docs, manifests, and module READMEs. Do not assume work is module-scoped.

Read every file you modify in full before editing. Do not remove, rename, or downgrade intentional functionality unless explicitly asked. Do not “fix” dependency or type problems by deleting behavior or weakening checks. Keep diffs tight; avoid unrelated refactors and formatting-only churn. After code changes, run repository validation commands required by `RULES.md`. Treat formatter, lint, warnings-as-errors, tests, and coverage as design constraints. Do not bypass hooks, checks, or validation steps.

Never use `--no-verify`. Never commit unless explicitly asked. If committing, commit only files changed in this session; use explicit paths when staging. Never use broad staging commands. Before committing, run `git status` and verify only intended files are staged. Include `fixes #<number>` or `closes #<number>` in commit message if related issue/PR exists.

Multiple agents may share a worktree; protect their changes. `git add <specific-file-paths>`
`git pull --rebase`
`git reset --hard`
`git clean -fd`
`git commit --no-verify`
Resolve conflicts only in files you changed. If conflict appears in untouched files, stop and ask user.

For issues, read the full issue including comments before acting; prefer complete reads over snippets. Analyze PRs before local changes. Do not open PRs, merge, or close anything unless explicitly asked.

Keep responses concise, direct, technical. No emojis in commits, issues, PR comments, or code comments unless explicitly asked.

Store transient context, scratch notes, logs, and task state under `.llm/{DIR}/`; choose `{DIR}` per task/agent to avoid collisions. Do not use `.context/` for new work. Treat `.llm/` as disposable, untracked working state; promote durable context into tracked docs explicitly.

`RULES.md` is canonical for definition of done, formatting/lint, warnings-as-errors, tests/coverage, and code size/complexity budgets. `WORKFLOW.md` defines issue, branch, PR, review, and merge workflow. `RELEASING.md` defines release, versioning, changelog, tagging, and publishing rules.
